`^([01]\d|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d$`

Breakdown:
- `^` … `$` — anchors the match to the whole line, so nothing else can ride along.
- `([01]\d|2[0-3])` — hours `00`–`19` via `[01]\d`, or `20`–`23` via `2[0-3]`. The split is what rejects `24:00`–`29:59`, which a naive `[0-2]\d` would let through.
- `:` — literal separator.
- `[0-5]\d` — minutes `00`–`59`, rejecting `60`+.

Two forks you may want to flip:
- **Zero-padded hours required** (as in your examples). If `7:45` should also match, use `^([01]?\d|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d$`.
- **`$` vs `\z`** — in most engines (Python, JS, PCRE) `$` also matches before a trailing newline, so `"07:45\n"` passes. If "the line, full stop" means no trailing newline either, use `\z` (Python/PCRE) or `\Z`/`$(?![\s\S])` depending on dialect.
